**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the booking filter match half-open windows**

When an existing booking ends exactly when the requested window begins (or starts exactly when it ends), the inclusive `gte`/`lte` predicates still fetch it. Because the subsequent sweep uses the booking's original interval rather than clipping it to the requested window, that non-overlapping reservation contributes its full quantity to `peakConcurrent`, potentially making a back-to-back booking appear to have no stock and blocking reservation or checkout. Use strict half-open overlap predicates (`from < window.to` and `to > window.from`) to match the sweep semantics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 779fb60b — `buildActiveBookingWhere` now uses strict half-open overlap (`from < window.to` / `to > window.from`) to match the end-exclusive peak-concurrent sweep, so a back-to-back booking that only touches the window no longer blocks it.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate only standalone quantities against the free pool**

When a draft contains a quantity-tracked kit slice, this aggregation treats that slice as a new request against `bookable`, even though `bookable` has already subtracted the same units through `inKits` and the availability query deliberately excludes kit-driven booking rows. For example, an asset whose entire quantity is allocated to a kit has `bookable = 0`, so reserving a booking containing that kit is rejected even though the kit owns the allocation. Exclude `assetKitId != null` slices from this free-pool guard, while still validating any standalone slice of the same asset.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 779fb60b — the reserve and update guards now validate only standalone (`assetKitId IS NULL`) slices against the free pool. Kit slices draw from their kit's allocation, already subtracted via `inKits`, so they're no longer double-counted.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude kit-inherited custody from the pool deduction**

When a kit holding this asset is assigned custody, Shelf creates `Custody` rows with a non-null `kitCustodyId`; this unfiltered aggregation counts those rows as `inCustody`, while the same availability result also subtracts the corresponding `AssetKit.quantity` as `inKits`. The shared batch primitive therefore double-deducts kit units, understates picker and booking availability, and can produce false stock conflicts. Filter custody to `kitCustodyId: null`; the same unfiltered custody aggregation should also be corrected in the singular availability and stock-lowering paths.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 779fb60b — custody is filtered to `kitCustodyId: null` in `computeAvailableQuantity`, the batch primitive, the stock-lowering guard, and the stock-conflict detector, so kit-inherited custody is no longer double-deducted alongside `inKits`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve directional checks for existing quantity edits**

When `updateBookingAssets` is used by the manage-assets route to reduce an existing quantity, this item omits `currentQuantity`, so the shared guard defaults it to zero and treats every submission as an increase. If the booking is already over-committed—for example, reducing 8 units to 7 while other reservations leave only 5 bookable—the reduction is rejected, recreating the over-reservation dead-end that the directional guard is intended to fix. Fetch and pass the existing standalone row quantity for updates, while retaining zero for genuinely new rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 779fb60b — `updateBookingAssets` fetches and passes each asset's existing standalone quantity as `currentQuantity`, so reducing an already-over-committed booking via manage-assets is allowed (the #2725 directional rule).
